article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: Pittsburgh's defense won the day without Aaron Rodgers, two Sunday games lost their starting quarterbacks, and the board flipped all three of its cards.

items.headline: Steelers 27, Broncos 5 — Pittsburgh's defense wins the day without Rodgers
paragraphs: Mason Rudolph started at quarterback in Pittsburgh's first game since the Steelers released Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, and the defense did the rest. T.J. Watt recovered a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone for a touchdown, and Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception for another score.
The Broncos managed five points in the rain at Acrisure Stadium. Denver falls to 8-4. Pittsburgh moves to 7-4 and has won the week twice over — first the Rodgers saga, then the game.
The Friday game is done. There is nothing to bet after the fact — the Sunday cards are where the action is now.
items.takeaway: A backup quarterback, a wet field, and a defense that scored twice. Sunday is the next live board.

items.headline: Injury board: two Sunday starters ruled out, and Watson still waits
paragraphs: Brock Purdy is out for Sunday against Seattle. The 49ers ruled him out Friday with a mid-ankle sprain suffered against Minnesota, and Mac Jones will start. Jones started eight games for San Francisco last season and won five of them. Wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable with an Achilles injury, and linebacker Dre Greenlaw is questionable with a neck injury.

Seattle gets its starter back: Sam Darnold returns after rib and quadriceps injuries. The Seahawks will be without right tackle Abraham Lucas, left guard Quenton Nelson, and defensive tackle Jarran Reed.

Justin Herbert is out for Sunday against New England. The Chargers ruled him out Friday with a concussion, and DJ Uiagalelei will start. The Patriots are down a quarterback too — Drake Maye is out with a fibula injury, so Tommy DeVito starts, and wide receiver A.J. Brown is doubtful with a hamstring injury.

Christian Watson is still in the concussion protocol after the hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens on Wednesday night. Green Bay does not play again until Sunday, Dec. 6, against New Orleans, so he has time to clear it.
items.takeaway: Two Sunday games changed quarterbacks today, and the board has already caught up — see what it means below.

items.headline: Rain coming Sunday in Cincinnati and Cleveland
paragraphs: The Saints at the Bengals kicks off at 1:00 p.m. ET in Cincinnati with rain expected and temperatures around 50. The Raiders at the Browns kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET in Cleveland with rain expected and temperatures in the upper 40s.
Rain is also possible in San Francisco for the Seahawks at the 49ers at 4:25 p.m. ET. The rest of Sunday's outdoor games look dry, and the dome games are indoors either way.
items.takeaway: Wet weather is a fact to know for Sunday, not a totals edge on its own.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board flipped all three cards — and it already has the new quarterbacks
paragraphs: The evening board is not the morning board. The Hit Rate card is now Cleveland on the moneyline at -230 on FanDuel, Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET. The Balanced card is now Indianapolis +5.5 at -105 on FanDuel. The Value lane has no play tonight.

The quarterback changes are already in the board. Mac Jones is listed as San Francisco's expected starter, and DJ Uiagalelei is listed as the Chargers' expected starter. The cards above are priced on the backups, not on the starters who were ruled out.

Hit Rate is the card that looks most likely to win, and it gives up value to get there. The app puts Cleveland's win chance around 64% against a market that says about 67%, at -230. That is a Hit Rate card doing its job — likeliest winner, not best price. The app's own tutorial says it plainly: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced is the middle ground. Indianapolis +5.5 at -105 is close to a coin flip the app will take — but only to +5.5 at -108. If your book shows a worse price than that, the app says no bet on the same team.
Value having no play is not a no on every game. It means no offer cleared the Value bar tonight. When a lane is empty, Check is how you test your own number.
items.takeaway: New quarterbacks, new cards. The board moved with the news — read the cards as they are now, not as they were this morning.

items.headline: The play-through price: the worst price the app still calls a bet
paragraphs: Every card on the board carries a play-through price. It is the worst price the app still calls a bet. Better than the play-through, the card stands. Worse than it, the app says no bet — same team, same game, different answer.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical. Say the board shows a card at -120 with a play-through of -123. Your book shows -110. That is a better price than the card, so the app would still say bet. But if your book shows -130, that is worse than the play-through, and the app says no bet.
That is why two people can look at the same card and get different answers. The price you can actually get is part of the bet, not an afterthought.
items.takeaway: A card is not just a team — it is a team at a price. Check your price against the play-through before you bet.

items.headline: The backup quarterbacks moved two lines — and the board moved with them
paragraphs: Seattle at San Francisco flipped favorites. This morning San Francisco was -3.0 on DraftKings and -152 on the moneyline. Tonight Seattle is -1.5 on DraftKings at -104, and San Francisco is +101 on the moneyline. The total came down from 43.5 to 42.5.

New England at the Chargers moved the other way. This morning New England was -2.5 on DraftKings and -1.5 on FanDuel. Tonight New England is -3.0 on both books. The moneyline went from -137 to -152 on DraftKings and -120 to -154 on FanDuel.

The Giants at the Colts moved too. Indianapolis was +6.5 on FanDuel this morning — the old Value card. Tonight it is +5.5, and the card moved lanes with it: Indianapolis is now the Balanced card at +5.5 and -105, good only to -108.
Cincinnati came in a half point, from -10.0 to -9.5 on DraftKings, and the Saints-Bengals total dropped from 49.5 to 48.5. Denver-Pittsburgh lines are off the board now that the game is final.

If your book is slow to move and still shows a morning number, tap Check and type it in. The app runs your price back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on the number you can actually get.
items.takeaway: Two backup quarterbacks moved two lines. If your book still shows the old number, Check it before it disappears.

items.headline: Check your number tonight — a good number now beats a hoped-for number Sunday
paragraphs: Sunday inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff, and that is the last hard news before the games. But the number you want may not wait that long. The Sunday late rush on big-name teams can push a line past the app's playable number.
If your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
The board refreshes every morning and evening. Check back in the morning for the final word before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Check your number tonight. If it is good and Check says bet, take it — do not wait for Sunday to move it against you.

evidence.fact: Pittsburgh beat Denver 27-5 on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in the first game since the Steelers released Aaron Rodgers; Mason Rudolph started at quarterback and the Steelers defense scored two touchdowns.
evidence.interpretation: A backup-quarterback team won big at home in the rain. The result is final and there is nothing to bet after the fact.
evidence.app_guidance: No card was on this game. The Sunday cards are where the action is now.

evidence.fact: Brock Purdy (ankle) was ruled out Friday for Sunday's game against Seattle; Mac Jones will start at quarterback for San Francisco. Purdy missed practice all week with a mid-ankle sprain suffered against Minnesota.
evidence.interpretation: The 49ers play their biggest home game of the season so far with their backup quarterback. Jones started eight games for San Francisco last season and won five.
evidence.app_guidance: Check whether the board's expected starter for San Francisco has flipped to Mac Jones before trusting the Hit Rate card at face value; if it has not, run Check on your own number.

evidence.fact: Justin Herbert (concussion) was ruled out Friday for Sunday's game against New England; DJ Uiagalelei will start at quarterback for the Los Angeles Chargers. Drake Maye (fibula) is out for New England, so Tommy DeVito starts for the Patriots.
evidence.interpretation: Both teams start backup quarterbacks on Sunday in Los Angeles. The Chargers are 1-9.
evidence.app_guidance: Check whether the board's expected starter for the Chargers has flipped to DJ Uiagalelei before trusting the Balanced card at face value; if it has not, run Check on your own number.

evidence.fact: Christian Watson is still in the concussion protocol after the hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens on Wednesday night. Green Bay does not play again until Sunday, Dec. 6, against New Orleans.
evidence.interpretation: No change since the morning brief. Watson has time to clear the protocol before Green Bay's next game.
evidence.app_guidance: Watson is a next-week question, not a Sunday question.

evidence.fact: Rain is forecast for Sunday in Cincinnati (Saints at Bengals, 1:00 p.m. ET, around 50 degrees) and Cleveland (Raiders at Browns, 8:20 p.m. ET, upper 40s), with rain also possible in San Francisco (Seahawks at 49ers, 4:25 p.m. ET). The other Sunday outdoor games look dry.
evidence.interpretation: Wet weather is a fact to know for Sunday, not a totals edge on its own.
evidence.app_guidance: Know the weather before kickoff, then let the app's number do the talking.
